LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION (CAPITAL LETTERS AND THE FULL STOP)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and the full stop)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and the full stop), part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use capital letters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (capital letters and the full stop) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn- The learner’s ability to learn independently is developed as they practise writing their names/names of their friends starting

with capital letters.

• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to write clearly improves as they use capital letters and the full stop correctly.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as learners work in groups collaboratively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem): A learner’s esteem is nurtured as they use target punctuation correctly in writing.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies knowledge about capital letters and the full stop when learning concepts in learning areas in other learning areas.

Suggested learning resources

• Textbooks in appropriate print and colour contrast

• Braille reference materials

• Audio recording

• Digital devices with assistive technology
